item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the better merge because its implementation exactly follows the required repository pattern: build the replayable multipart body with multipartbody.NewFile and delegate to FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B preserves Add as the single path for FilesOption handling, request construction, response decoding, and error semantics.","A explicitly violates the frozen contract by duplicating Add's option processing, Raw.Do call, payload decoding, and missing-data handling inside Upload.","Both implementations validate filename/content and propagate multipartbody.NewFile errors, but B does so with substantially less duplicate machinery.","A has stronger multipart/retry assertions and validation coverage, but those test advantages do not outweigh its architectural contract violation."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses Add despite an explicit requirement to route through it, creating behavior-drift and maintenance risk.","The new Add documentation makes broad claims about silently skipped retries and specific reader types that may become inaccurate as transport behavior evolves.","Tests do not cover source-reader failures and use bytes.NewReader rather than a genuinely streamed source."],"risks_b":["Tests omit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases required by the contract.","The retry test does not verify that multipart content is present and intact on the second attempt, so it could miss an empty replayed body.","The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods: true as in the reported POST-retry scenario, and Upload lacks a Go doc comment."]}
